identity.title: Nuchal rigidity, Kernig and Brudzinski signs

technique.how: Supine patient. Nuchal rigidity: passively flex the neck chin-to-chest; positive if resistance or inability to touch chin to chest. Kernig: hip flexed 90 degrees, extend the knee; positive if extension is resisted/painful before 135 degrees. Brudzinski: passive neck flexion produces involuntary hip and knee flexion.
technique.prerequisites: No suspected cervical spine injury; patient able to cooperate at least partially.
technique.contraindications: Suspected cervical spine trauma or instability.

interpretation.positive_finding: Meningeal irritation possible, but in prospective ED/inpatient cohorts the signs barely change the probability of CSF pleocytosis (LR+ around 1); nuchal rigidity was sensitive only with severe pleocytosis (>=1000 WBC).
interpretation.negative_finding: Does not exclude meningitis: sensitivity 5% for Kernig/Brudzinski and 13-30% for nuchal rigidity. Never withhold LP or antibiotics on the basis of absent signs.
interpretation.pitfalls: Elderly, immunosuppressed and obtunded patients often lack signs; cervical spondylosis, parkinsonism and neck pain from other causes mimic rigidity.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive: increases urgency for LP/empiric therapy only modestly; negative: changes nothing, decide on LP from fever, headache, AMS and risk factors.

sources.citation: Thomas KE, Hasbun R, Jekel J, Quagliarello VJ. The diagnostic accuracy of Kernig's sign, Brudzinski's sign, and nuchal rigidity in adults with suspected meningitis. Clin Infect Dis 2002;35:46-52.
Nakao JH, Jafri FN, Shah K, Newman DH. Jolt accentuation of headache and other clinical signs: poor predictors of meningitis in adults. Am J Emerg Med 2014;32:24-28.
Attia J, Hatala R, Cook DJ, Wong JG. The rational clinical examination. Does this adult patient have acute meningitis? JAMA 1999;282:175-181.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Never use absent signs to defer LP or antibiotics when meningitis is clinically plausible; avoid neck flexion with possible cervical injury.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Fever plus headache plus AMS, petechial rash, or immunosuppression mandates empiric antibiotics and LP regardless of meningeal signs.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Thomas 2002 signs were elicited by examining clinicians before LP; Nakao 2014 used a physician questionnaire completed before CSF results. Attia RCE notes Kernig assessed in only one study and Brudzinski in none since the original report.

extraction_notes: Thomas 2002 (CID) is not OA, so specificity, LR- and prevalence are null and location is the abstract; the RCE (Attia 1999) predates Thomas and has no pooled LR for these signs so it is cited as context only. Nakao 2014 LRs computed from rounded whole-percent sens/spec and are therefore crude (Brudzinski LR+ ranges 0.7-1.3 depending on rounding). Nakao prevalence 47/230 = 0.20 from abstract. Entry 1 quote spans Kernig and Brudzinski; the target_condition of each entry names the sign.
